name: cto
install_doc: `npm install -g claude-token-optimizer`, then `cto init` in the project. The hooks step is `cto hooks install --all` (here `cto init --yes --hooks`, its documented non-interactive form), then pasting the block `cto hooks settings` prints into the project's .claude/settings.json. The second setup command is that paste. `cto init --yes` writes CLAUDE.md, .claude/{COMMON_MISTAKES,QUICK_START,ARCHITECTURE_MAP}.md, docs/INDEX.md and .claudeignore.
notes: AS SHIPPED, THE GUARD HOOKS DO NOTHING. They read the tool name from $CLAUDE_TOOL_NAME, and Claude Code 2.1.325 never sets it (no occurrence in the binary, checked 2026-11-14), so each guard exits before acting. This arm measures that state, because that is what a user installs; cto-patched measures the hooks working. CLAUDE.md is the template `cto init --yes` generates. cto ships no command that fills it, and writing project facts into it ourselves would be our content rather than theirs.
